newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks close higher, led by Ganadero.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks close higher, led by Ganadero.

text.p: Colombian stocks closed higher in active trade fueled by demand for bank shares, including blue-chip Banco Ganadero, and buying interest in brewer Bavaria S.A.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index closed up 0.45 percent at 13,413.10 on above-average trading volume of 2.2 billion pesos. Bogota's IBB closed up 0.86 percent, meanwhile, ending the day at 866.07 on a volume of 1.5 billion pesos.
The day's biggest winner by far was Banco Ganadero, whose preferential shares jumped 12.5 percent in Medellin to end at 225 pesos a share.
Medellin-based bank Bancoquia finished a close second, however, rising 9.67 percent in Bogota to close at 1,700 pesos per share.
Other gainers included Banco de Bogota, which rose 2.28 percent in Medellin to close at 5,830 pesos a share and Bavaria, which ended up 3.15 percent on the day in Medellin at 3,920 pesos a share.
Banco de Colombia, the country's second-largest bank in terms of assets, closed up 1.11 percent in Bogota at 455 pesos per share.
Ordinary shares of Banco Ganadero, Colombia's biggest bank in terms of assets, ended up just 1.26 percent in Bogota at 280.50 pesos a share -- failing match the huge gain in its preferential shares.
Brokers have said there was a clear interest on the part of some investors in narrowing the spread between Ganadero's preferential and ordinary shares, however.
Large cross-trades in the shares of cement manufacturer Cementos Argos and cigarette maker Coltabaco contributed to the trading volume in Bogota but both companies closed unchanged.

Corfinsura, a financial arm of the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno industrial group, closed up 2.70 percent in Medellin at 1,900 pesos a share and the group's Suramericana de Seguros insurance company ended up 1.09 percent at 18,500 pesos per share. -- Javier Mozzo, Bogota newsroom, 571 610 7944
